chapters.summary: Carmelita Lopa, assistant at a group family daycare in East Flatbush, describes payment reversals, late payments, and a $2,300 violation she says was issued during COVID despite a passing inspection. She also notes losing children due to 2K/3K hour changes.
chapters.title: Carmelita Lopa testifies on payment reversals and violations

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So my name is Carmelita Lopa.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: I'm an educator and provider.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: I'm actually the assistant of my program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: My sister is the on-site provider.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Our facility is a group family daycare.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: It's called Habawasanigu Academy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: That comes from the Garifuna language.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: We're located in East Flatbush.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: I am a member of POP and NYCC.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Some concerns which bring me here today, which I heard echoed before, are payment issues.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So in reporting payments, sometimes we get paid three to four weeks after the fact, which in turn causes a problem for payroll.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Or we have reversed payments.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So the payment is given and then taken away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: It might be the next check or whatever, and then I'll have to cover the funds.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: It's just ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So an example of that is if, say, the child were being paid on a regular rate and it was a special needs child.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: It's the craziest thing, but they take back the payment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: And then I have to wait until it's adjusted five to six weeks later.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So that's definitely something that is crazy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So if universal child care is supposed to be available for all children, then...

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: be a city priority.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: It needs to figure out how to adjust that system to reflect the dilemma that we have.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Another problem that we have is with the 2K and the 3K, the change in hours.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: Some parents cannot pick up their children at 2 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: If not, that means them losing their job, their employment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So we lost four children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: To that.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: And then we were able to get them back because I figured out a way to pick up those four children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa
utterances.text: So for another provider, that would just be a loss.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Carmelita Lopa

chapters.summary: Sheba Kapoor of the New York State Montessori Alliance asks the subcommittee to recognize median age for mixed-age classrooms and to accept accredited Montessori credentials for lead teacher positions in 3K and pre-K.
chapters.title: Sheba Kapoor testifies on Montessori education

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Hi, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chairs Gutierrez and Thomas Henry.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Thank you so much for the opportunity to offer testimony on behalf of the New York State Montessori Alliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Montessori education serves over 15,000 students and employs more than 1,000 Montessori teachers across New York State, and many of those schools are in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: And we educate children as young as infants and toddlers in licensed child care centers through 12th grade in public, independent, and religious schools.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: We respectfully ask the subcommittee to consider two important policy changes.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Recognizing median age as an appropriate method for determining predominant age in mixed-age classrooms,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: and recognizing accredited Montessori teacher education credentials as a pathway to qualification for lead teacher positions in 3K and pre-K programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: A defining feature of Montessori education is the mixed-age classroom.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Children typically remain with the same teacher and community for multiple years, learning alongside peers at different developmental stages,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: and we therefore urge the city to recognize the median age of enrolled children as an appropriate method for determining a classroom's predominant age for purposes of applying the relevant staffing ratios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: This approach would allow Montessori schools to maintain established

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: mixed-age classroom structures and comply with applicable staffing requirements without unnecessarily disrupting children's continuity of care.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: And we ask the subcommittee to support regulatory guidance that explicitly permits the use of median age for predominant age determinations while preserving existing child safety protections and approved staffing ratios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: Our second request concerns Montessori teacher credentials.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: When these credentials are not adequately recognized, experienced and appropriately prepared Montessori educators may face barriers to employment in publicly supported early childhood programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Sheba Kapoor
utterances.text: We respectfully ask the city to establish a clear pathway for recognizing credentials issued by MACT accredited or American Montessori Society or Association.

chapters.summary: Ethan Chan, a father and community board member, testifies on the closure of Christ the King Community Daycare and Preschool. He asks the City Council to facilitate a succession plan and warns the closure will destabilize child care across Central and Western Queens.
chapters.title: Ethan Chan testifies on Christ the King closure

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Chair and members of the City Council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: My name is Ethan Chan, and I am testifying today as a father, a former member of Queens Community Board 5, and a current associate board member of South Asian Youth Alliance, Youth Action, SIA, and Elbers Queens, where I volunteer to support and mentor inner city youth.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I am a native New Yorker.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Child of immigrants, and the first in my family to attend college.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I was raised in New York City public schools, graduated from Brooklyn Technical High School, and earned my college and university degrees right here in New York City.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I chose to stay here to raise my sons and watch them thrive in the city that gave me everything.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Today, I am petitioning the City Council to urgently explore every option to keep Price the King Community Daycare

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: and preschool open beyond its announced closure date of July 1st, 2027.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I stated earlier, on October 27th, families were notified that after 30 years of dedicated service, Education Director Dorothy Wagner is retiring, and a decision was made to close the daycare, 3K, and pre-K program entirely.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I've already called

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Councilmember Phil Wong's office in District 1.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: 30 to raise my concerns, and I appreciate that his office has already asked the school to reconsider.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: However, we need the city council and city agencies to actively intervene and help facilitate a succession plan.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: While I fully understand and acknowledge the current enrollment crisis happening across all of education,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Fettering a foundational community institution is not the answer.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Established in 1993, Christ the King's Preschool and Daycare is a local pillar in Middle Village.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Crucially, its impact reaches far beyond the borders of Council District 30.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: The center serves as a vital anchor for working and residential families in Middle Village,

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Maspeth, Glendale, Elmhurst, Regal Park, and Forest Hills, who all want to remain in New York City and raise their next generation of kids.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Closing this program will destabilize child care across Central and Western Queens and cause many families to reconsider moving to or staying in our district and neighboring communities to raise our children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: For my family, the stakes are personal.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: My oldest son, Declan, completed both his daycare and pre-K years at Christ the King.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: I personally want the chance to see my younger son, Rowan, in his preschool years at Christ the King.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Ethan Chan
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Next, we'll hear from Jesse Gudo.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry

chapters.summary: Jesse Guido, a Maspeth resident and father, testifies that Christ the King is a trusted 'unicorn' program and implores the committee to keep it open.

utterances.text: I'm a resident of Maspeth, Middle Village area, and I won't take up too much of your time.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido
utterances.text: My concern is identical to the previous speakers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido
utterances.text: As a parent, you want to have your children, especially when they're that age, in trusted hands.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido
utterances.text: You need to know that they're going to be in a place where not only they can learn, flourish, and thrive, but you trust where they are.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido
utterances.text: There's not an ounce or a minute that goes by every day where I worry about my child's well-being and whereabouts in that facility.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido
utterances.text: And I implore you to do everything in your power to try to leave it open.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Jesse Guido

chapters.summary: Mary Ayinde of St. Nick's Alliance and Small World Early Childhood Center testifies on three priorities: strengthen the early childhood workforce, pay providers the real cost of care, and invest in regulatory agencies. She criticizes the enrollment-based funding model.
chapters.title: Mary Ayinde testifies on Small World Early Childhood Center

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Good afternoon and thank you Chairman Gutierrez and members of the New York City Council Subcommittee on Early Childhood Education.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: I'm calling from the center of Small World Early Childhood Center, which is operated by St.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Nick's Alliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: As North Brooklyn Settlement House and Civic Anchor, St.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Nick's Alliance provides diverse, multi-generational services for very young children to the elderly also, including our 50-year-old center, Small World.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: As an early childhood provider, St.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Nick's Alliance Testimonial.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: focuses on three critical improvements essential to stabilizing the early childhood ecosystem, and that would be one, strengthen the early

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: childhood education workforce.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Number two, pay providers the real cost of operating early childhood education centers.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: And number three, invest in regulatory agencies.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: For community-based providers, hiring and retaining early childhood staff is extremely difficult due to low salaries, which are a direct result of inadequate contract values set by the New York City Department of Education

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: and ratified by DC 37's Local 95 and Local 205 contracts.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Center-based providers such as small work cannot afford to offer salary parity with similar positions working directly at the DOE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: And as a result, center-based providers face very high vacancy rates and staff shortages, preventing them from running at full capacity due to Article 47 child to adult ratios.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Under paying providers the real cost of operating early childhood centers, the birth to five contract must be completely overhauled.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: The current enrollment-based model is highly defective with no guarantee of covering the real fixed cost for operating centers, such as rent, insurance, and Article 47 safety regulations that do not change based on enrollment.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: This funding model also ignores that center-based providers have very little control over enrollment as the system is centralized under DOE.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Under invest in regulatory agencies.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Your time has expired.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Mary Ayinde
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you for your testimony.

chapters.summary: Rita Wentworth, head of Pine Street School and president of the New York State Montessori Alliance, testifies on teacher qualification requirements. She says Article 47 does not consistently recognize Montessori training and asks for equitable pathways and consistency across regulatory frameworks.
chapters.title: Rita Wentworth testifies on Montessori teacher qualifications

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Good afternoon, chairpersons and members of the council.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: I am the head of school at Pine Street School in Lower Manhattan, president of the New York State Montessori Alliance.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Before I begin, I want to express my heartfelt sympathy to the school community that shared its experience of an unexpected closure.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: I cannot speak to the circumstances of that closure, but I know how difficult it is to sustain an early childhood program.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: When a school closes, children, families, and educators lose a community they depend on, and it reminds us how fragile even deeply committed schools can become.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: I'm here to address how teacher qualification requirements affect our ability to recruit exceptional educators and sustain early childhood programs.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Under Article 47, group teacher requirements do not consistently recognize rigorous Montessori training as an independent qualification.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: We encounter exceptional Montessori-trained educators, sometimes with master's degrees in other disciplines, who must complete additional requirements to qualify.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Alternatively, we hire teachers who meet the city's qualifications and invest significant resources training them in our educational philosophy.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: What's more, teachers themselves face substantial investments of time and money in additional coursework, often without a clear financial return, and there is a significant issue of parity.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: A preschool operating under Article 43 can face different and less teacher qualification requirements than a standalone early childhood program under Article 47, even when both are serving the same children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: We are educating the same children.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: at the same developmental stages, yet our regulatory classification can determine which educators are eligible to teach them.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: At a time when we desperately need talented early childhood educators, these inconsistencies risk turning them away.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: And this is a business sustainability issue.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Prolonged vacancies increase recruitment and training costs, strain existing staff, and can limit enrollment even when families need spaces.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: With staffing already our greatest expense, these costs cannot continually be absorbed or passed on through higher tuition.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: We are not asking for lower standards.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: We are asking for equitable pathways that recognize rigorous professional preparation and greater consistency across regular frameworks.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Rita Wentworth
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Shanel Thomas-Henry
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Annie Lintonberg, a Middle Village resident and parent, testifies on the closure of Christ the King Community Daycare Preschool. She says the center has served her family for decades and asks for honest answers about why it is closing.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annie Lintonberg

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annie Lintonberg
utterances.text: This isn't simply the loss of a school.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annie Lintonberg
utterances.text: It's a potential loss of an entire early childhood education community, including trusted teachers, established classrooms, developmental support, and child care arrangements that working families depend on.

utterances.speaker: Member of the Public - Annie Lintonberg
